name: Galitzenklamm
kurzbeschreibung: Galitzenklamm near Lienz captivates visitors with a roaring water gorge trail since 1885, Southern Austria's only stone ball mill, and via ferratas.
beschreibung:
Overview

The wildly romantic Galitzenklamm lies at the foot of the steeply towering Lienzer Dolomiten in the East Tyrolean municipality of Amlach, just under three kilometers southwest of the sunny town of Lienz. Situated at the confluence of the roaring Galitzenbach and the Drau, this natural monument combines a spectacular historic water trail with a modern climbing and family adventure park. Over millennia, the mountain stream carved deep gorges and giant potholes into the hard dolomite rock, creating a fascinating natural setting of thunderous cascades, sheer cliffs, and crystal-clear water.

Natural Monument & Attractions

The tourist development of the natural gorge boasts a long tradition: the first wooden walkway for visitors was constructed as early as 1885. Today, an elaborately secured water trail leads along sturdy wooden bridges, suspension walkways, and spectacular viewing platforms right beside the roaring waterfalls. Educational boards provide information on flora, fauna, and the geological characteristics of the Lienzer Dolomiten. A cultural-historical rarity at the gorge exit is the historic Steinkugelmühle: as the only operating water-powered stone ball mill in all of southern Austria, it harnesses the untamed water power of the mountain stream to grind rough dolomite rocks into perfectly round stone spheres over days of milling. For climbing enthusiasts, Galitzenklamm ranks among the top destinations in the Eastern Alps: five via ferratas in various difficulty levels—from the easy family via ferrata (grade B/C) to the extremely demanding sports via ferrata Dopamin (grade E)—are carved directly into the vertical gorge walls. An extensive water playground featuring a rope ferry, mud play area, and climbing elements completes the family offering.

Visit & Getting There

Galitzenklamm is open daily from early May to late October from 09:00 to 18:00 (extended until 19:00 in July and August; weather-related closures possible during storms). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults €9.50, children aged 6 to 14 €7.00, small children under 6 free; family ticket €25.00. Admission is free with the regional Osttirol Card. Via ferrata equipment can be rented directly at the ticket counter. Arrival by bicycle: the gorge is located directly on the supra-regional Drauradweg R1 and can be easily reached from Lienz in about 15 minutes by bike. By car: via the Drautalstraße B100 to Lienz, then follow the signs for Amlach / Galitzenklamm to the large free parking area on the gorge grounds (Galitzen 1). By public transport: ÖBB train to Lienz station, then bus line 962 to Amlach or by rental bike along the Drau.

Tips

The entrance area with the Steinkugelmühle, water playground, and snack station is completely flat and easily accessible with strollers and wheelchairs; the gorge trail itself traverses steps and metal gratings and requires sturdy footwear. After the visit, the sun terrace of the Jausenstation Galitzenklamm invites visitors to enjoy traditional East Tyrolean Schlipfkrapfen and refreshments overlooking the roaring waterfalls.
